notes: HAND-OFF FOR THE SIBLING CHAIN: Run identifier TR-9062, project PR-2005 (v1 int 379335744). No numeric/uuid id is exposed anywhere in the create response, the list response, or the run-test-cases response for this run - identifier (TR-9062) is the only id this v2 surface returns for a run, confirming list_test_runs_v2's own guidance that its serializer emits no id/uuid. If a numeric run id is ever needed downstream, it will have to come from get_test_runs_v1 (v1 listing), not from anything in this v2 chain. EXACT ARGUMENTS THAT WORKED (attempt 3): path_params {project_id: 'PR-2005'}, body flat (NOT wrapped in test_run) = {name, assignee, run_state, tags, test_cases: ['TC-54457','TC-54458','TC-54455','TC-54456']} - test_cases must be bare TC-NNN strings, NOT {test_case_id: ...} objects as the contract's own field list implies (this contradicts the capability's own declared param shape - a drift in the REQUEST contract, not just the response). CASES ATTACHED (verified via get_test_run_test_cases_v2, all 4 present, all untested, no configuration): TC-54457 (numeric 1972036, from __scratch__ folder 764138) and TC-54458 (numeric 1975349, from __scratch__ child folder 764828) are the writable scratch cases. TC-54455 (numeric 1971631) and TC-54456 (numeric 1971632) from the __readonly__ pool were ALSO attached to broaden the row count for assign_test_run_test_cases_v2 and bulk_update_test_run_test_cases_v2 - attaching them created run-owned test-run-test-case records (row/mapping ids = latest_result_id: TC-54455->2150387253, TC-54456->2150387251, TC-54457->2150387252, TC-54458->2150387254); downstream status/assignee writes on these rows modify only those records, never the underlying __readonly__ cases TC-54455/TC-54456 themselves - do not write to those cases directly. Numeric case ids were only recoverable from each row's 'urls.self' field (pattern .../test-runs//<numeric_case_id>/<latest_result_id>), same pattern previously seen for plans and cases. run_state='new_run' (explicit, matches default), active_state='active' (only value observed, taken from the response, not invented), assignee='ing@bsstag.com' (resolved successfully, stored and echoed back as a STRING - not the object shape the nested response schema declares), tags=['mcp-probe'] (round-tripped intact), configurations=[] (none requested, none returned), no test_plan_id/sub_test_plan_id sent so no plan linkage - the response's filter_test_cases:{is_dynamic:false} appeared even though no filter/plan fields were sent, meaning this key is unconditionally present on every v2 run, not just dynamic ones. RESPONSE IS READ FROM STORAGE, NOT AN ECHO: create's response test_run has fewer fields than what was sent (e.g. no test_cases field at all, confirming population is a separate, asynchronous step) and the identical object shape reappeared verbatim on the later list_test_runs_v2 read (steps 4), so this is genuinely persisted state, not a client-side echo. STANDING LESSON CONFIRMATIONS: (1) json_path/wrapper - this capability's own guidance says 'every field goes inside a test_run object', but invokeCapability rejects a literally-nested body client-side ('unknown body: test_run...'); the correct call is flat, and the server re-applies /test_run/<field> internally (attempt 2's validator errors surfaced as #/test_run/test_cases/N, proving the re-nesting happens server-side after the client sends flat). (2) The declared request shape for test_cases (array of {test_case_id} objects) is wrong - the real API wants an array of bare TC-NNN strings; sending objects is a 400 'Invalid JSON data'. (3) Response drift is severe: 15 declared nested-schema fields are absent (id, uuid, type, owner, environment, overall_progress, overall_progress_by_status_id, test_cases_count, is_automation, observability_url, metadata, assignee_imported, is_dynamic, test_plans, self_ui_link, links.detail), while filter_test_cases and urls (plus links.test_cases) are returned undeclared by the nested schema - the flat 'returns' array partially covers filter_test_cases/urls but not the nested nested-schema fields that are missing, reconfirming the standing lesson that the flat returns array disagrees with both the nested schema and reality in both directions. (4) assignee is declared as a nested object {id, browserstack_user_id, full_name, group_id, onboarded} in the response schema but is actually returned as a plain email string - a type-shape mismatch. All three attempts and both post-create verification reads are recorded above; verdict is DRIFT given the large declared/actual disagreement on the response shape and the wrong declared request shape for test_cases, even though the run was successfully created and verified to exist with all 4 cases attached.
